engXBook: Who is the person who writes the story in a book?
The author is the person who writes the words of a book.
Who makes the drawings that go with the story?
The illustrator creates the pictures in a book.
Which part of a book holds the pages together and shows on a bookshelf?
The spine is the edge of a book you see when it stands on a shelf.
Where is the title of a book usually found?
The title is printed on the front cover so readers can find the book.
What do we call the paper sheets inside a book that we read?
The words and pictures of a book are printed on its pages.
When you finish reading a book, which part do you close?
The back cover is at the end of the book, so you close it when you finish.
Mia reads the words by Robert Munsch on the cover. Who is Robert Munsch?
The word by before a name tells us who wrote the book.
A book cover says Pictures by Michael Martchenko. Who is Michael Martchenko?
Pictures by tells us who drew the illustrations.
What tells you what a book is called?
The title is the name of the book.
Which way do you turn the pages in an English book?
From right to left, front to back
From the back to the front
English books are read from front to back, turning each page from right to left.
Where do you begin reading the words on a page?
In English we start reading at the top left of the page.
Which way do your eyes move when you read a line of English words?

"The bus is here," said Mom, "grab your bag."
"The bus is here," said Mom. "grab your bag."
"The bus is here" said Mom. "Grab your bag."
These are two separate sentences, so a period follows Mom and the second quote starts with a capital.
Which sentence is formatted correctly?
Did the coach really say, "No practice today"?
Did the coach really say, "No practice today?"
Did the coach really say "no practice today"?
Did the coach really say, "No practice today".
The whole sentence is the question, not the quote, so the question mark goes outside.
Which sentence is formatted correctly?
"Look out!" yelled the lifeguard.
"Look out"! yelled the lifeguard.
"Look out!", yelled the lifeguard.
"Look out!" Yelled the lifeguard.
The exclamation mark goes inside the quotation marks and no comma is added.
Which sentence is formatted correctly?
My brother whispered, "I'm scared of the dark."
My brother whispered "I'm scared of the dark."
My brother whispered, "i'm scared of the dark."
My brother whispered, "I'm scared of the dark".
A comma introduces the quote, it starts with a capital and the period goes inside.
Which sentence is formatted correctly?
"After lunch," said Mr. Roy, "we will go outside."
"After lunch," said Mr. Roy, "We will go outside."
"After lunch" said Mr. Roy "we will go outside."
"After lunch," said Mr. Roy. "we will go outside."
The interrupted sentence uses commas around the speaker tag, and the second part stays lowercase.
Which sentence is formatted correctly?
"Where is my hat?" asked Ben. "I left it here."
"Where is my hat?" asked Ben, "I left it here."
"Where is my hat"? asked Ben. "I left it here."
"Where is my hat?" Asked Ben. "I left it here."
The question mark goes inside, asked is lowercase and a period separates the two sentences.
Which sentence is formatted correctly?
Sara said, "The library opens at nine."
Sara said, "the library opens at nine."
Sara said "The library opens at nine".
Sara said, "The library opens at nine".
A comma introduces the quote, it begins with a capital and the period goes inside.
Which sentence is formatted correctly?
"Hurry up," said Dad, "or we'll miss the ferry."
"Hurry up," said Dad, "Or we'll miss the ferry."
"Hurry up" said Dad, "or we'll miss the ferry."
"Hurry up," said Dad "or we'll miss the ferry."
Commas surround the speaker tag in a split quote, and or continues the sentence in lowercase.
Which sentence is formatted correctly?
"I finished my book," Zoe announced.
"I finished my book." Zoe announced.
"I finished my book", Zoe announced.
"I finished my book," zoe announced.
A comma inside the quotes ends the spoken part when the sentence continues.
Which sentence is formatted correctly?
The sign said, "Keep off the ice."
The sign said "keep off the ice."
The sign said, "Keep off the ice".
The sign said, Keep off the ice."
A comma introduces the quoted words, which begin with a capital and end with the period inside.
Which sentence is formatted correctly?
"Can I help?" asked Mia. "I'm good at puzzles."
"Can I help?" asked Mia, "I'm good at puzzles."
"Can I help"? asked Mia. "I'm good at puzzles."
"Can I help?" asked Mia. "i'm good at puzzles."
Each spoken sentence is punctuated inside its quotes, and a period separates them.
Which shows the correct way to write a conversation between two people?
Start a new paragraph each time the speaker changes.
Write both speakers' words in the same paragraph.
Put each speaker's words in italics.
Use a new paragraph only when the topic changes.
Starting a new paragraph for each new speaker helps readers follow who is talking.
Which word in this sentence should be capitalized? "we're going camping," said Ella.
we're
said
camping
going
The first word of a quotation is capitalized, so we're should be We're.
Where does the comma go? "I'm ready" said Omar.
Inside the quotation marks after ready
Outside the quotation marks after ready
After said
After Omar
Commas that end a quoted statement go inside the closing quotation marks.
Which sentence is formatted correctly?
"Wow!" said Kai. "That's a huge moose!"
"Wow"! said Kai. "That's a huge moose!"
"Wow!" said Kai, "that's a huge moose!"
"Wow!" Said Kai. "That's a huge moose!"
Each exclamation goes inside its quotes, said is lowercase and a period separates the two sentences.
Which sentence is formatted correctly?
Ms. Park asked, "Who wants to read first?"
Ms. Park asked, "Who wants to read first"?
Ms. Park asked "who wants to read first?"
Ms. Park asked, "Who wants to read first?".
The quoted words are the question, so the question mark goes inside and nothing follows it.
engXMnTw: Text 1: Beavers build dams across streams using branches and mud. Text 2: Beaver dams create ponds that give fish, frogs and birds a place to live. Which sentence combines the main ideas of both texts?
Beavers build dams that create ponds where many animals live.
Beavers have sharp teeth.
Frogs live in ponds.
Mud is found near streams.
It joins Text 1's idea (beavers build dams) with Text 2's idea (the ponds become homes).
Text 1: The Trans-Canada Highway was finished in 1962. Text 2: The highway connects all ten provinces, from Newfoundland to British Columbia. Which sentence combines the main ideas of both texts?
The Trans-Canada Highway, finished in 1962, links all ten provinces.
Newfoundland is an island.
Highways have many cars.
British Columbia is in the west.
It combines when the highway was built with what it connects.
Text 1: Monarch butterflies lay their eggs only on milkweed plants. Text 2: Milkweed is disappearing as fields are turned into farms and roads. Which sentence combines the main ideas of both texts?
Losing milkweed puts monarch butterflies at risk.
Butterflies are orange.
Farms grow crops.
Roads are made of asphalt.
It connects the monarch's need for milkweed with the loss of milkweed.
Text 1: Reading every day builds a bigger vocabulary. Text 2: Kids who read often also do better at writing. Which sentence combines the main ideas of both texts?
Reading every day improves both vocabulary and writing.
Books have many pages.
Writing takes time.
Libraries are quiet.
It brings together both benefits of reading from the two texts.

Text 1: The Northern Lights appear when particles from the sun hit Earth's atmosphere. Text 2: Yellowknife is one of the best places in the world to see the Northern Lights. Which sentence combines the main ideas of both texts?
Particles from the sun create Northern Lights that can be seen well in Yellowknife.
The sun is a star.
Yellowknife is cold in winter.
Lights are bright at night.
It combines what causes the lights with where to see them.
Text 1: Plastic bags often end up in oceans. Text 2: Sea turtles mistake floating bags for jellyfish and eat them. Which sentence combines the main ideas of both texts?
Plastic bags in the ocean are dangerous for sea turtles.
Jellyfish float in the sea.
Turtles have shells.
Bags carry groceries.
It links plastic in oceans with the harm to turtles.

Text 1: Laura Secord walked about 30 kilometres in 1813 to warn British soldiers of an American attack. Text 2: Her warning helped the British and Mohawk forces win the Battle of Beaver Dams. Which sentence combines the main ideas of both texts?
Laura Secord's long walk to warn the British helped win the Battle of Beaver Dams.
Laura Secord liked walking.
Battles happened in 1813.
Soldiers wore uniforms.
It combines her journey (Text 1) with its result (Text 2).
Text 1: Trees take in carbon dioxide from the air. Text 2: Cities are planting more trees to fight climate change. Which sentence combines the main ideas of both texts?
Cities plant trees because trees remove carbon dioxide from the air.
Cities have tall buildings.
Air is invisible.
Trees have leaves.
It connects what trees do with why cities plant them.
Text 1: Canada has more lakes than any other country. Text 2: These lakes hold about one-fifth of the world's fresh surface water. Which sentence combines the main ideas of both texts?
Canada's many lakes hold a large share of the world's fresh water.
Lakes are good for swimming.
Water is wet.
Canada is a big country.
It combines the number of lakes with how much water they hold.
Text 1: Sleep helps your brain store what you learned during the day. Text 2: Students who sleep nine hours do better on tests. Which sentence combines the main ideas of both texts?
Getting enough sleep helps students remember and do well on tests.
Beds are comfortable.
Tests are hard.
Brains are inside skulls.
It links how sleep helps memory with better test results.
Text 1: Salmon are born in rivers and then swim to the ocean. Text 2: Years later, they return to the same river to lay their eggs. Which sentence combines the main ideas of both texts?
Salmon travel from rivers to the ocean and back again to lay eggs.
The ocean is salty.
Rivers flow downhill.
Fish have fins.
It combines both parts of the salmon's journey.
Text 1: The Inuit invented the qajaq, a light boat made of skin stretched over a frame. Text 2: Today's kayaks are based on the qajaq design. Which sentence combines the main ideas of both texts?
Modern kayaks come from a boat the Inuit invented.
Boats float on water.
Skin can be stretched.
Kayaks are colourful.
It links the Inuit invention with the modern kayak.
Text 1: Bike lanes give cyclists a safe space on the road. Text 2: Cities with bike lanes have fewer cycling injuries. Which sentence combines the main ideas of both texts?
Bike lanes make cycling safer.
Roads are busy.
Bikes have two wheels.
Cities are large.
It joins what bike lanes do with the safety result.
Text 1: Volcanoes erupt when melted rock pushes up through Earth's crust. Text 2: Mount Meager in British Columbia erupted about 2400 years ago. Which sentence combines the main ideas of both texts?
Canada has volcanoes, like Mount Meager, that erupt when melted rock pushes up.
Rocks are hard.
British Columbia has mountains.
Volcanoes are hot.
It combines how eruptions happen with a Canadian example.
Text 1: Vegetables contain vitamins your body needs. Text 2: Eating colourful vegetables can help you fight off colds. Which sentence combines the main ideas of both texts?
Vegetables give your body vitamins that help keep you healthy.
Carrots are orange.
Colds make you sneeze.
Vitamins come in pills.
It joins both texts' ideas about how vegetables help health.
Text 1: Wind turbines make electricity from moving air. Text 2: Some towns in Prince Edward Island get much of their power from wind farms. Which sentence combines the main ideas of both texts?
Wind turbines turn wind into electricity that powers towns in Prince Edward Island.
Wind can be strong.
Prince Edward Island is small.
Electricity is useful.
It combines how turbines work with where they are used.
Text 1: Snowshoe hares have brown fur in summer. Text 2: In winter their fur turns white to match the snow. Which sentence combines the main ideas of both texts?
Snowshoe hares change fur colour with the seasons to blend in.
Hares have long ears.
Snow is cold.
Summer is warm.
It combines both seasons into one main idea about camouflage.
Text 1: Music lessons teach children to read notes and keep rhythm. Text 2: Studies show music practice can also improve memory and focus. Which sentence combines the main ideas of both texts?
Music lessons build musical skills and also help memory and focus.
Pianos have keys.
Practice takes time.
Notes are written on paper.
It joins the musical and the thinking benefits.
Text 1: Honey never spoils if it is sealed well. Text 2: Archaeologists found honey in ancient Egyptian tombs that was still safe to eat. Which sentence combines the main ideas of both texts?
Sealed honey lasts so long that ancient honey can still be eaten.
Egypt is hot.
Bees make honey.
Tombs are old.
It links the fact that honey does not spoil with the ancient example.

Text 1: The Rideau Canal was built in the 1830s to move troops and supplies. Text 2: Today it is used for boating in summer and skating in winter. Which sentence combines the main ideas of both texts?
The Rideau Canal was built for the military but is now used for fun all year.
Skating is a winter sport.
Boats float.
Troops carry supplies.
It combines the canal's original purpose with its present use.
Text 1: Recess gives students time to run and play. Text 2: Teachers notice students pay better attention after recess. Which sentence combines the main ideas of both texts?
Recess lets students be active, which helps them focus in class.
Playgrounds have swings.
Teachers work hard.
Running is fast.
It joins the activity of recess with its effect on attention.
Text 1: Bats eat thousands of insects every night. Text 2: Farmers save money on pesticides when bats live near their fields. Which sentence combines the main ideas of both texts?
Bats help farmers by eating insects that harm crops.
Bats sleep upside down.
Insects have six legs.
Farms are in the country.
It combines what bats eat with how that helps farmers.
engXThSs: Nora wanted to quit piano because the new song was too hard. Her teacher told her to practise one line a day. Two months later, Nora played the whole song at the recital. What is the theme of the story?
Hard work and patience help us reach difficult goals
Nora succeeds by practising a little each day, showing that patience and effort pay off.
Jae teased his little brother for being afraid of the dark. Then a storm knocked out the power, and Jae was the one who wanted a flashlight. What is the theme of the story?
Everyone has fears, so we should not mock others
Jae learns he has fears too, which shows that teasing others for their fears is unfair.

Three friends each wanted to build a different kind of fort. They argued until it got dark. The next day, they combined their ideas and built the best fort on the street. What is the theme of the story?
Working together creates better results than arguing
The friends succeed only when they cooperate, so the message is about teamwork.
Lily told everyone she had a pet tiger. When her classmates asked to visit, she had to admit it was a cat. Nobody believed her stories after that. What is the theme of the story?
Lily's lie leads to people no longer believing her, showing that lies damage trust.
A young spruce tree wished it were as tall as the old pines. When a strong wind snapped the tall pines, the little spruce bent and survived. What is the theme of the story?
Being small or different can be a strength
Pines are taller than spruce trees
The spruce's smallness saves it, so the theme is that what seems like a weakness can be a strength.
Omar spent all his allowance on candy the first day. When the school fair came that weekend, he had nothing left to spend. What is the theme of the story?
Planning ahead with money is wise
Candy is bad for your teeth
Omar's choice leaves him with nothing later, teaching the value of planning.
Grandma could not hear well, so Maya learned sign language. Their talks became the best part of Maya's week. What is the theme of the story?
Making an effort to understand others strengthens relationships
Maya's effort brings them closer, which is the story's message.
The team's best player, Cole, never passed the puck. The team kept losing. When Cole started passing, they won the championship. What is the theme of the story?
A team succeeds when everyone shares
The team wins only after Cole shares the puck, showing that teamwork matters.
Hana thought the new girl, Elise, was stuck-up because she never talked. Later Hana learned Elise was just shy and had moved from Québec. They became good friends. What is the theme of the story?
Don't judge people before you get to know them
Hana's first judgment was wrong, so the theme is to get to know people before judging.
A crow could not reach the water at the bottom of a jar. It dropped pebbles in one by one until the water rose high enough to drink. What is the theme of the story?
The crow solves its problem by thinking creatively.
Ben laughed when his friend tripped on stage. The next week, Ben forgot his lines, and his friend helped him instead of laughing. What is the theme of the story?
Treat others the way you want to be treated
Ben experiences kindness after being unkind, which shows the golden rule.

Every winter, the village shared its food with an old woman who lived alone. One spring, a flood came, and she showed them a safe path up the mountain that only she knew. What is the theme of the story?
Kindness often comes back to us
The village's kindness is returned when she saves them.

Ali wanted the newest phone because all his friends had one. When he finally got it, he realized he still felt left out because his friends were busy playing games instead of talking. What is the theme of the story?
The phone does not fix his loneliness, showing that possessions cannot replace connection.
Zara entered the art contest and did not win. Instead of giving up, she kept painting every day. The next year, her painting hung in the town library. What is the theme of the story?
Zara keeps trying after losing and succeeds later.
The ant worked all summer storing food while the grasshopper sang. When winter came, the grasshopper was hungry and the ant was warm and fed. What is the theme of the story?
It is wise to prepare for the future
Singing is a waste of time
The ant's planning protects it in winter, so the theme is preparing ahead.
Theo always picked the same seat on the bus. One day it was taken, so he sat beside a boy he didn't know. That boy became his best friend. What is the theme of the story?
Trying something new can lead to good surprises
A change Theo didn't choose leads to friendship, showing the value of new experiences.
Ivy found a baby bird on the ground. She wanted to keep it, but her dad explained it needed its parents. She watched from the window as the mother bird returned. What is the theme of the story?
Ivy shows care by leaving the bird with its family.

The king offered gold to whoever brought the most beautiful flower. Many brought fake flowers. Only one girl brought an empty pot, admitting her seed had not grown. The king made her his heir. What is the theme of the story?
The girl is rewarded for telling the truth, showing honesty matters most.
Mateo was embarrassed by his dad's accent. At the school culture fair, his dad told stories about growing up in Chile, and Mateo's classmates loved them. What is the theme of the story?
We should be proud of where we come from
Mateo learns his family's background is something to be proud of.
Two brothers raced to finish their chores first. They rushed so much that they broke a vase and had to spend the afternoon cleaning up. What is the theme of the story?
Rushing can make things take longer
Hurrying caused more work, so the theme is that rushing backfires.
Rain fell on the town's picnic day. Instead of going home, everyone moved into the community centre, played board games and had the best picnic ever. What is the theme of the story?
A positive attitude can turn problems into good times
The town makes the best of bad weather, showing the power of a positive attitude.
Sami kept his mistakes on the math test secret from his parents. The next test went even worse. When he finally asked for help, his marks improved. What is the theme of the story?
Asking for help is a sign of strength
Sami improves only after asking for help, showing it is wise to seek help.
engXAuPM: Wolves live and hunt in groups called packs. Each pack has its own territory, which can cover hundreds of square kilometres. What is the author's purpose and message?
To inform readers about how wolves live
To persuade readers to adopt a wolf
To entertain readers with a wolf adventure
To describe how to draw a wolf
The passage gives facts about wolf packs, so it is meant to inform.
Our school should have a longer lunch recess. Students would get more exercise, and they would come back to class ready to focus. What is the author's purpose and message?
To persuade readers that recess should be longer
To inform readers about the history of recess
To entertain readers with a recess story
To explain how to play tag
The author states an opinion and gives reasons, so the purpose is to persuade.
Penguin Pete wanted to fly. He flapped and flapped, then belly-flopped into the ocean — and discovered he was the fastest swimmer in the colony. What is the author's purpose and message?
To entertain readers and show that everyone has their own talents
To inform readers about how penguins swim
To persuade readers to visit a zoo
To explain why birds can fly
It is a funny story with a lesson about finding your own strengths.
Wash your hands for at least 20 seconds with soap. It's the easiest way to stop germs from spreading. Do it before every meal! What is the author's purpose and message?
To persuade readers to wash their hands well
To entertain readers with a story about soap
To inform readers about where germs come from
To describe different kinds of soap
The commands and the word easiest urge readers to act, so it persuades.
The Canadarm was a robotic arm built in Canada. It flew on the space shuttle and helped astronauts move satellites and equipment in space. What is the author's purpose and message?
To inform readers about a Canadian invention used in space
To persuade readers to become astronauts
To entertain readers with a space adventure
To explain how to build a robot
It presents facts about the Canadarm, so it informs.
Grandpa's old truck coughed, sputtered and finally rolled into town with a pumpkin in the passenger seat wearing a seatbelt. What is the author's purpose and message?
To entertain readers with a silly scene
To inform readers about how trucks work
To persuade readers to buy pumpkins
To explain seatbelt safety
The funny image of a buckled-up pumpkin is meant to amuse readers.
Please don't feed the ducks bread. Bread fills them up but has no nutrients, and leftover bread makes ponds dirty. Bring peas or oats instead. What is the author's purpose and message?
To persuade readers to feed ducks healthier food
To inform readers about the history of ponds
To entertain readers with a duck story
To explain how bread is made
The author asks readers to change what they do and gives reasons, so it persuades.
Mira was too nervous to try out for the choir. Her best friend held her hand on the way to the audition. Mira sang beautifully and made the choir. What is the author's purpose and message?
To entertain readers and show that friends give us courage
To inform readers about how choirs work
To persuade readers to join a choir
To explain how to audition
It tells a story whose message is that support from friends helps us be brave.
Hummingbirds can flap their wings up to 80 times per second. They are the only birds that can fly backward. What is the author's purpose and message?
To inform readers about amazing facts about hummingbirds
To persuade readers to plant flowers
To entertain readers with a hummingbird tale
To describe how to feed birds
It shares facts, so its purpose is to inform.
Every family should have an emergency kit with water, a flashlight and a first-aid kit. Storms can knock out power for days. Be prepared! What is the author's purpose and message?
To persuade readers to prepare an emergency kit
To inform readers about how storms form
To entertain readers with a storm story
To describe what a flashlight is
Should and Be prepared! show the author wants readers to act.

Viola Desmond refused to leave the whites-only section of a Nova Scotia theatre in 1946. Her stand helped start the fight for equal rights in Canada, and today she appears on the ten-dollar bill. What is the author's purpose and message?
To inform readers about Viola Desmond and show how one brave act can bring change
To persuade readers to go to the theatre
To entertain readers with a funny story
To explain how money is printed
It gives historical facts and shows the lasting effect of her courage.
The snowman winked at Leo. "Don't tell anyone," it whispered, "but I'm planning to escape to the North Pole before spring." What is the author's purpose and message?
To entertain readers with an imaginative story
To inform readers about how snow melts
To persuade readers to build snowmen
To explain where the North Pole is
A talking snowman is made up and fun, so the purpose is to entertain.
Turn off lights when you leave a room. It saves electricity, lowers your family's bills and helps the environment. Every switch counts! What is the author's purpose and message?
To persuade readers to save electricity
To inform readers about how light bulbs work
To entertain readers with a story about a lamp
To describe different kinds of light switches
The author urges readers to act and lists reasons, so it persuades.
Kenji's kite got stuck in a tree. Instead of crying, he and his sister built a new one from newspaper and string. It flew even higher. What is the author's purpose and message?
To entertain readers and show that problems can lead to creative solutions
To inform readers about how kites fly
To persuade readers to recycle newspaper
To explain how trees grow
The story is enjoyable and its message is about solving problems creatively.
A blue whale's heart is about the size of a small car. Its tongue can weigh as much as an elephant. What is the author's purpose and message?
To inform readers about how huge blue whales are
To persuade readers to protect elephants
To entertain readers with a whale adventure
To explain how to measure a car
It shares facts about blue whales, so it informs.
Kids should read for fun every day. Reading builds your imagination, teaches new words and is a great way to relax before bed. What is the author's purpose and message?
To persuade readers to read every day
To inform readers about how books are printed
To entertain readers with a bedtime story
To describe the parts of a library
The author's opinion and reasons are meant to convince readers.
Fluffy the cat decided she was in charge of the house. She sat on homework, napped on keyboards and glared at anyone who sat in her chair. What is the author's purpose and message?
To entertain readers with a funny description of a bossy cat
To inform readers about cat breeds
To persuade readers to adopt a cat
To explain how to train a cat
The humorous details are meant to amuse readers.
The Bluenose was a famous fishing and racing schooner from Lunenburg, Nova Scotia. It won many races and appears on the Canadian dime. What is the author's purpose and message?
To inform readers about a famous Canadian ship
To persuade readers to go sailing
To entertain readers with a pirate story
To explain how coins are made
It gives facts about the Bluenose, so it informs.
Litter in parks hurts animals and makes places ugly. Pick up after yourself and carry a bag for trash. Let's keep our parks beautiful! What is the author's purpose and message?
To persuade readers to keep parks clean
To inform readers about animals in parks
To entertain readers with a story about a park
To describe the plants in a park
The author gives reasons and calls readers to action.

Old Mr. Fisher had no family, so the kids on his street visited him each Sunday. They played cards and listened to his sailing stories. He said they were the treasure he never found at sea. What is the author's purpose and message?
To entertain readers and show that friendship can be a treasure
To inform readers about sailing
To persuade readers to play cards
To explain how to find treasure
The story's message is that the kids' friendship is precious to Mr. Fisher.
Earthworms make soil healthier. As they tunnel, they let air and water reach plant roots, and their waste adds nutrients. What is the author's purpose and message?
To inform readers about how earthworms help soil
To persuade readers to go fishing
To entertain readers with a worm adventure
To explain how to plant seeds
The passage explains facts about earthworms, so it informs.
Wear a helmet every time you ride your bike. Helmets reduce the risk of serious head injuries. It only takes a second to buckle up! What is the author's purpose and message?
To persuade readers to wear bike helmets
To inform readers about how bikes are built
To entertain readers with a bike race story
To describe different helmet colours
The command and reasons are meant to persuade readers to stay safe.
engSmMt: Is this a simile or a metaphor? The lake was as smooth as glass.
It compares the lake to glass using as, so it is a simile.
Is this a simile or a metaphor? My little brother is a tornado.
It says the brother is a tornado without like or as, so it is a metaphor.
Is this a simile or a metaphor? She swims like a fish.
It uses like to compare her to a fish, so it is a simile.
Is this a simile or a metaphor? The road was a ribbon winding through the hills.
It says the road was a ribbon directly, so it is a metaphor.
Is this a simile or a metaphor? His hands were as cold as ice.
It uses as … as to compare, so it is a simile.
Is this a simile or a metaphor? Dad is a bear in the morning.
It says Dad is a bear without like or as, so it is a metaphor.
Is this a simile or a metaphor? The baby slept like a log.
It uses like to make the comparison, so it is a simile.
Is this a simile or a metaphor? The snow was a thick white quilt on the field.
It calls the snow a quilt directly, so it is a metaphor.
Is this a simile or a metaphor? The runner was as quick as a cheetah.
It uses as … as, so it is a simile.
Is this a simile or a metaphor? Her eyes were bright stars.
It says her eyes were stars without like or as, so it is a metaphor.
Is this a simile or a metaphor? The thunder sounded like a drum.
It uses like to compare thunder to a drum, so it is a simile.
Is this a simile or a metaphor? The library is a treasure chest of stories.
It calls the library a treasure chest directly, so it is a metaphor.
Is this a simile or a metaphor? The kitten was as light as a feather.
It uses as … as, so it is a simile.
Is this a simile or a metaphor? The sky was a blue canvas.
It says the sky was a canvas without like or as, so it is a metaphor.
The clouds looked like cotton balls.
The clouds danced across the sky.
The playground was an oven in July.
The playground was as hot as an oven.
The playground felt like an oven.
The playground was very hot in July.
It says the playground was an oven without like or as.
Her laugh was like bells ringing.
Her laugh could be heard for kilometres.
It uses like to compare her laugh to bells.
The moon was a lantern in the sky.
The moon was like a lantern.
The moon was as bright as a lantern.
The moon was full and bright.
It calls the moon a lantern directly.
The hallway was as dark as a cave.
It uses as … as to compare the hallway to a cave.
My teacher is a walking dictionary.
My teacher is like a dictionary.
My teacher is as smart as can be.
It says the teacher is a dictionary directly.
Which word tells you this is a simile? The puppy's fur was soft like velvet.
Similes use like or as to compare two things.
The leaves fell like golden rain.
It uses like to make the comparison.
engFgSp: What does this mean? Her room was a pigsty.
Her room was very messy.
Her room had pigs in it.
Her room was on a farm.
Her room was very small.
Comparing a room to a pigsty means it is extremely messy.
What does this mean? He was as cool as a cucumber during the test.
He stayed calm during the test.
He felt cold during the test.
He ate a cucumber during the test.
He was nervous during the test.
Cool as a cucumber means calm and relaxed.
What does this mean? The exam was a breeze.
The exam was very easy.
The exam was held outside.
The exam was very long.
The exam was confusing.
Calling something a breeze means it was easy and effortless.
What does this mean? My legs were jelly after the race.
My legs felt weak and shaky.
My legs were sticky.
My legs felt strong.
My legs were sweet.

engTpHi: The Klondike Gold Rush An original passage written for LearnAce 1 In August 1896, Skookum Jim, Dawson Charlie and George Carmack found gold in Bonanza Creek, in what is now Yukon. Sophie was jealous of her sister. When her sister got a new bike, Sophie crossed her arms and muttered, "It's not fair." Which detail shows Sophie's jealousy?
Complaining that it is not fair shows she wishes she had what her sister got.
The puppy was full of energy. It raced around the yard, leapt at butterflies and never stopped wagging its tail. Which detail supports the idea that the puppy was energetic?
Racing around shows the puppy has lots of energy.
Kenji was honest. When the cashier gave him too much change, he walked back into the store to return it. Which detail supports that Kenji is honest?
Giving back money that wasn't his shows honesty.
The forest was peaceful. Sunlight drifted through the leaves, a stream trickled softly and birds sang quietly. Which detail best supports the idea that the forest was peaceful?
A soft, gentle sound like a trickling stream creates a peaceful mood.
Amara was a hard worker. She delivered newspapers before dawn every day for a year to save for a laptop. Which detail shows Amara's hard work?
She delivered newspapers before dawn every day for a year
Getting up early every day for a year shows dedication and effort.
Uncle Ray was a joker. He hid rubber spiders in the cereal box and wore a fake moustache to dinner. Which detail supports the idea that Uncle Ray is a joker?
He hid rubber spiders in the cereal box
Hiding fake spiders is a prank, which shows he likes to joke.
The town was deserted. Shop windows were boarded up, weeds grew through the sidewalk and not a single car passed. Which detail best supports that the town was deserted?
No traffic at all shows that no one is around.
Leah was shy. At the party, she stood by the wall, staring at her shoes, and answered questions in a whisper. Which detail shows that Leah is shy?
She answered questions in a whisper
Speaking only in a whisper shows she feels shy around others.
Hamid was responsible. Every night, he fed the family's goats, locked the barn and checked the water trough before bed. Which detail supports that Hamid is responsible?
He fed the goats and locked the barn every night
Doing his chores carefully every night shows responsibility.
The old ship was in poor shape. Its sails were torn, its paint was peeling and water leaked through cracks in the hull. Which detail best supports the idea that the ship was in poor shape?
Water leaked through cracks in the hull
A leaking hull shows the ship is badly damaged.
Mira was generous with her time. Every Saturday, she read stories to seniors at the care home and helped them write letters. Which detail shows Mira's generosity?
She read stories to seniors every Saturday
Seniors live at the care home
Giving up her free time to help others shows generosity.
Coach Bell was strict. Players who showed up late had to run three laps, and no one could leave practice early. Which detail supports that Coach Bell is strict?
Late players had to run three laps
A firm punishment for lateness shows strictness.
Ava felt proud. She held up her science fair ribbon, grinned and showed it to everyone who walked by. Which detail shows Ava's pride?
She showed the ribbon to everyone who walked by
Showing off her ribbon to everyone shows she is proud.
The village was poor. Children walked barefoot, roofs were patched with scraps of tin and families shared a single well. Which detail best supports that the village was poor?
Roofs were patched with scraps of tin
Patching roofs with scraps shows people could not afford proper materials.
Theo was clever. When the canoe sprang a leak, he plugged the hole with a ball of chewing gum and kept paddling. Which detail shows that Theo is clever?
He plugged the leak with chewing gum
Solving a sudden problem with what he had shows cleverness.
Ms. Duval was caring. When a student cried during the test, she knelt beside him, spoke gently and gave him extra time. Which detail supports that Ms. Duval is caring?
She knelt beside the student and spoke gently
Comforting an upset student shows that she cares.
engXSdInf: Wetlands protect communities from floods. Like giant sponges, they soak up heavy rain and release it slowly. Which detail supports the idea that wetlands protect against floods?
They soak up heavy rain and release it slowly
Wetlands are home to frogs
Some wetlands are called marshes
Wetlands can be muddy
Holding rainwater and letting it go slowly is how wetlands prevent floods.
Camels are well suited to the desert. They can go for days without drinking, and their wide feet keep them from sinking into the sand. Which detail best supports the main idea?
Their wide feet keep them from sinking into sand
Camels can be brown
Deserts are hot
People ride camels
Wide feet that help in sand show how camels are built for the desert.
Helmets save lives. Studies show that wearing a bike helmet greatly lowers the risk of a serious head injury in a crash. Which detail supports the idea that helmets save lives?
Helmets greatly lower the risk of serious head injuries
Helmets come in many colours
Bikes have two wheels
Some people ride to school
Reducing serious head injuries is evidence that helmets protect lives.
The Arctic is warming quickly. Sea ice now melts earlier in spring and forms later in fall than it did fifty years ago. Which detail supports the main idea?
Sea ice melts earlier and forms later than before
Polar bears live in the Arctic
The Arctic has long winters
Ice is frozen water
Changes in the timing of sea ice are evidence of warming.
Octopuses are clever animals. In aquariums, some have learned to unscrew jar lids to reach food inside. Which detail supports the idea that octopuses are clever?
Some have learned to unscrew jar lids
Octopuses have eight arms
They live in the ocean
Aquariums have tanks
Solving a problem like opening a jar shows intelligence.
Music lessons can help children in school. Researchers have found that students who learn an instrument often do better at remembering information. Which detail supports the main idea?
Students who learn an instrument often remember information better
Pianos have black and white keys
Some children like to sing
Music can be loud
Better memory is evidence that music lessons help in school.
Canada has a huge coastline. At more than 240 000 km, it is the longest coastline of any country in the world. Which detail best supports the main idea?
It is the longest coastline of any country
Canada has ten provinces
Oceans are salty
Canada has many lakes
Being the longest coastline in the world proves it is huge.
Snow can keep small animals warm. Mice and voles tunnel under the snow, where the temperature stays near 0°C even when the air above is much colder. Which detail supports the main idea?
The temperature under the snow stays near 0°C
Mice are small
Snow is white
Voles eat seeds
A steady, milder temperature under the snow shows how snow keeps animals warm.
Trees help cool cities. On hot days, streets shaded by trees can be several degrees cooler than streets with no trees. Which detail supports the idea that trees cool cities?
Shaded streets can be several degrees cooler
Some trees lose their leaves
Cities have many buildings
Streets need sidewalks
Measured cooler temperatures under trees support the main idea.
Dogs can help people who are blind. Guide dogs are trained to stop at curbs and lead their owners around obstacles. Which detail supports the main idea?
Guide dogs stop at curbs and lead owners around obstacles
Dogs have a strong sense of smell
Some dogs are large
Puppies need training
Stopping at curbs and avoiding obstacles shows how guide dogs help.
The Rocky Mountains are still changing. Each year, wind, water and ice wear away tiny bits of rock from their peaks. Which detail supports the main idea?
Wind, water and ice wear away rock each year
The Rockies are in Alberta and British Columbia
Some peaks have snow
Many people hike there
Ongoing erosion is evidence that the mountains are still changing.
Screen time before bed can make sleep worse. The bright light from phones and tablets can make it harder for the brain to feel sleepy. Which detail supports the main idea?
Bright screen light makes it harder to feel sleepy
Tablets have touch screens
Many people own phones
Bedtime is at night
Light that blocks sleepiness explains how screens hurt sleep.
Ants work together as a team. Some ants gather food, some care for the young and others defend the nest. Which detail supports the idea that ants work as a team?
Different ants do different jobs for the colony
Ants are very small
Ants have six legs
Some ants are red
Sharing jobs across the colony shows teamwork.
Composting reduces garbage. Food scraps and yard waste make up a large part of what households throw away, and they can be turned into soil instead. Which detail supports the main idea?
Food scraps and yard waste can become soil instead of garbage
Gardens need soil
Garbage trucks are big
Some people eat salads
Turning a large part of household waste into soil means less garbage.
Salmon make an amazing journey. Many swim hundreds of kilometres upstream, even leaping up waterfalls, to return to the stream where they hatched. Which detail best supports the main idea?
They leap up waterfalls to return to where they hatched
Salmon are a kind of fish
Bears eat salmon
Streams have fresh water
Swimming far and leaping waterfalls shows how amazing the journey is.
Hummingbirds use a lot of energy. Their wings can beat more than 50 times per second, so they must eat often. Which detail supports the main idea?
Their wings can beat more than 50 times per second
Hummingbirds are colourful
They drink nectar from flowers
Some live in gardens
Beating wings so quickly takes a great deal of energy.
Sunscreen protects your skin. It blocks harmful ultraviolet rays that can cause sunburn. Which detail supports the idea that sunscreen protects skin?
It blocks harmful ultraviolet rays
Sunscreen comes in bottles
The beach is sunny
Summer is warm
Blocking UV rays that cause sunburn is how sunscreen protects skin.
Libraries offer more than books. Many lend out musical instruments, run coding clubs and offer free internet. Which detail supports the main idea?
Many lend instruments and run coding clubs
Libraries are quiet
Books have pages
Some libraries are old
Lending instruments and running clubs are services beyond books.
The CN Tower was once the tallest free-standing structure in the world. It stands 553 metres high and held that record for more than 30 years. Which detail supports the main idea?
It held the height record for more than 30 years
It is in Toronto
Visitors can eat at the top
It was finished in the 1970s
Holding the record for decades supports the claim that it was once the tallest.
Exercise improves mood. During exercise, the body releases chemicals called endorphins that help people feel happier. Which detail supports the main idea?
Exercise releases endorphins that help people feel happier
Running shoes have laces
Some people exercise at a gym
Soccer is a team sport
Endorphins explain how exercise lifts mood.
Wolves help keep ecosystems balanced. When wolves returned to Yellowstone Park, elk stopped overeating young trees along rivers, and the trees grew back. Which detail best supports the main idea?
The trees grew back after wolves returned
Wolves live in packs
Elk are large animals
Yellowstone is a park
The return of the trees shows how wolves restored balance.
Learning a second language has benefits. People who speak two languages can often switch between tasks more easily. Which detail supports the main idea?
Bilingual people can often switch between tasks more easily
French is spoken in Quebec
Some words are long
Many languages use an alphabet
Switching tasks more easily is a benefit linked to knowing two languages.
engPlgR: Which of these is plagiarism?
Copying a paragraph from a website and handing it in as your own
Quoting a sentence in quotation marks with a citation
Summarizing an article in your own words and citing it
Stating a common fact like "Canada has ten provinces"
Presenting someone else's words as your own without credit is plagiarism.
Which of these is acceptable use?
Paraphrasing a book in your own words and citing it
Changing a few words in a copied paragraph without citing it
Handing in a friend's essay with your name on it
Using a photo from a website without credit
Putting ideas in your own words and naming the source gives proper credit.
Maya copied a sentence from an encyclopedia into her report but forgot to cite it. What is the best way to fix this?
Put the sentence in quotation marks and cite the encyclopedia
Change one word in the sentence
Move the sentence to the end of the report
Make the sentence bold
Quotation marks and a citation show the words belong to the encyclopedia.
Liam used ideas from a magazine article but wrote them in his own words. What else must he do to avoid plagiarism?
Cite the magazine article as his source
Nothing, because he used his own words
Add more words to each sentence
Put every sentence in quotation marks
Ideas from a source still need credit, even when paraphrased.
Which of these is plagiarism?
Using a chart from a report without saying where it came from
Crediting a chart below it with the report's name
Making your own chart from survey data you collected
Writing a common fact without a citation
Charts and images are someone's work too, so they need credit.
Which of these is plagiarism?
Asking an older sibling to write your essay and handing it in as yours
Asking a sibling to check your spelling
Talking about ideas with a classmate before you write
Reading a book to learn about your topic
Handing in work someone else wrote is plagiarism.
Which of these does NOT need a citation?
A common fact, such as "The Sun rises in the east"
A direct quotation from a scientist
A statistic from a news article
A summary of an author's argument
Widely known facts do not need to be cited, but others' words, data and ideas do.
Noor found a perfect sentence online and changed only two words. Why is this still plagiarism?
The wording and idea still belong to the original writer
Because two words is too few to change
Because sentences from the internet are always false
It is not plagiarism if you change any words
Swapping a few words does not make someone else's sentence your own.
Which of these is the best paraphrase of "Beavers build dams to create ponds that protect them from predators" (cited)?
Beavers make ponds with their dams so they can stay safe from predators (Lee).
Beavers build dams to create ponds that protect them from predators.
Beavers build dams to make ponds that protect them from predators.
Beavers are rodents with flat tails.
It restates the idea in new words and gives the source.
Which of these is acceptable use?
Using a short quotation in quotation marks and naming the author
Copying a whole page and listing the source at the end
Copying a poem and signing your name under it
Taking a classmate's answers and rewording them
A short, clearly marked and credited quotation is acceptable.
Omar handed in the same project he made last year for a different class without asking. What is this called?
Self-plagiarism
Paraphrasing
Proper citation
Summarizing
Reusing your own old work without permission is a form of plagiarism.
Jade wrote her report using a website but did not keep track of where her facts came from. What should she do to avoid plagiarism next time?
Write down each source as she takes notes
Use only one sentence from each website
Avoid using any facts at all
Copy the facts exactly so they are correct
Recording sources while taking notes makes it possible to cite them later.
Which of these is plagiarism?
Using a song's lyrics in your poem without credit
Writing your own original poem about a song
Quoting a song lyric in quotation marks with the artist's name
Saying you like a certain song
Using someone's lyrics as if you wrote them is plagiarism.
Which of these is acceptable use?
Including a photo in a slideshow with a credit to the photographer
Using a photo and cropping out the photographer's name
Using a photo and saying you took it
Tracing a drawing and calling it your own
Giving the photographer credit is acceptable use.
What is the main purpose of a citation?
To give credit to the source of words or ideas
To make a report longer
To show you used big words
To prove you typed the report
Citations tell readers whose work you used.
Eli used a quotation but forgot the quotation marks, though he cited the source. What should he fix?
Add quotation marks around the exact words
Remove the citation
Change the words to capital letters
Nothing, because a citation is enough
Exact words need quotation marks as well as a citation.
Which is the best way to use a long paragraph from a book in your essay?
Summarize the main idea in your own words and cite the book
Copy the whole paragraph without quotation marks
Copy it and change every fifth word
Copy it and say a friend wrote it
A cited summary uses the ideas honestly and in your own voice.
Ana's group wrote a report together, but she handed it in with only her name on it. Why is this a problem?
She took credit for work others did
The report was too short
Group reports cannot have names
She used her own words
Claiming shared work as only your own is a form of plagiarism.
Which of these is plagiarism?
Copying answers from a website for a homework question and saying you wrote them
Using a website to check that your answer is right
Citing a website as the source of a fact
Reading a website to learn about a topic
Submitting copied answers as your own is plagiarism.
Which of these is acceptable use?
Using an idea from an interview and naming the person you interviewed
Using an interview and claiming the ideas were yours
Making up quotations from a real person
Copying a news interview without naming the newspaper
Naming the person gives credit for their ideas.
Kai's sentence reads: "Glaciers cover about 10 percent of Earth's land." He found this number in a science article. What should he add?
A citation to the science article
An exclamation mark
A drawing of a glacier
Nothing, since numbers are never cited
Specific statistics from a source must be cited.
Which of these is plagiarism?
Using an AI tool to write your essay and handing it in as your own work
Writing your essay yourself after reading several sources
Asking a teacher for help planning your essay
Using a dictionary to check a word's meaning
Submitting writing you did not create as your own work is plagiarism.
